clauses.text: (a) Hoops shall be provided in the following regions of frame members: (i) At both ends of the flexural member, over a length equal to twice the member depth measured from the face of the supporting member toward midspan; and (ii) Over lengths equal to twice the member depth, on both sides of a section where flexural yielding is likely to occur in connection with inelastic lateral displacements of the frame.
clauses.notes:
Hoops - closed transverse reinforcement loops provided to confine concrete and restrain longitudinal bars in a frame member.
Face of the supporting member - the surface of the column or wall at the end of the flexural member.
Flexural yielding - the condition where the section reaches its bending capacity, associated with inelastic response under lateral loads.
Inelastic lateral displacements - lateral movements of the frame beyond the elastic range, occurring during seismic events.

clauses.text: (b) For transverse reinforcement in flexural members of special moment frames, the first hoop shall be located not more than 50 mm from the face of the supporting member. Maximum spacing of the hoops shall not exceed the least of: (i) d/4, (ii) eight times the diameter of the smallest longitudinal bars, (iii) 24 times the diameter of the hoop bars, and (iv) 300 mm.
clauses.notes:
Hoop - closed transverse reinforcement provided in the critical regions of a flexural member.
Face of the supporting member - the surface of the column or wall at the end of the beam, from which the first hoop location is measured.
d - the effective depth of the flexural member cross-section.

clauses.text: (c) Where hoops are required in flexural members of special moment frames, longitudinal bars on the perimeter shall have lateral support conforming to Section 8.1.9.4(c). Where hoops are not required, stirrups with seismic hooks shall be spaced not more than d/2 throughout the length of the member.
clauses.notes:
Hoops - closed transverse reinforcement required in critical regions of a flexural member.
Stirrups with seismic hooks - open or closed transverse reinforcement with hooks meeting seismic detailing requirements, used where hoops are not required.
d - the effective depth of the flexural member cross-section.
Seismic hooks - hooks with geometry meeting seismic detailing requirements.

clauses.text: (d) Hoops in flexural members of special moment frames are allowed to be made up of two pieces of reinforcement consisting of a U-stirrup having hooks not less than 135° with an extension of 6 bar diameters but not less than 75 mm, anchored in the confined core, and a cross tie to make a closed hoop. Consecutive cross ties engaging the same longitudinal bar shall have their 90° hooks at opposite sides of the flexural member. If the longitudinal reinforcing bars secured by the cross ties are confined by a slab only on one side of the flexural frame member, the 90° hooks of the cross ties shall all be placed on that side.
clauses.notes:
Hoop - closed transverse reinforcement used to confine concrete and provide lateral support to longitudinal bars.
U-stirrup - a stirrup bent into a U-shape forming one piece of a two-piece hoop assembly.
Hook angle - the bend angle at the end of the U-stirrup, required to be not less than 135° for seismic detailing.
Confined core - the concrete enclosed within the hoops, into which the U-stirrup hooks must be anchored.
Cross tie - a straight bar with hooks at each end used to close the U-stirrup and complete the hoop.
Consecutive cross ties - cross ties placed one after another along the member length engaging the same longitudinal bar.
90° hooks - the hook end of the cross tie bent at 90°
